prompt:
Run DESeq2 differential expression on this synthetic count matrix, with three ctrl versus three treated replicates. This is a platform QA fixture, not a biological study.
gene,ctrl1,ctrl2,ctrl3,treat1,treat2,treat3
GENE1,100,120,110,200,210,195
GENE2,50,55,48,52,49,51
GENE3,30,28,32,90,88,95
GENE4,200,210,195,205,198,202
GENE5,15,18,16,45,50,48
GENE6,80,85,78,82,79,81
GENE7,10,12,11,35,38,33
GENE8,300,310,295,308,302,296
GENE9,25,27,24,70,75,68
GENE10,60,65,58,63,59,62

data.text:
**nf-core/differentialabundance — DESeq2 differential expression analysis on raw count matrix with contrast-based statistical testing.**

- **Input:** Inline count matrix (10 genes × 6 samples: ctrl1–3 vs treat1–3)
- **Key steps:**
  - DESeq2 normalization (median-of-ratios) + dispersion estimation → normalized counts + size factors
  - Wald test (treatment vs control contrast) → log2 fold-changes + p-values + adjusted p-values (Benjamini-Hochberg)
- **Expected output:** 
  - `results.csv` — gene-level statistics (baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj)
  - `ma_plot.png` — M-A plot (log-ratio vs log-intensity)
  - `pca_plot.png` — PCA biplot of normalized counts
  - `results_shrunken.csv` — apeglm log2FC shrinkage (reduces noise on low-count genes)

The workflow is configured for your synthetic QA fixture with default parameters (alpha=0.05 for significance threshold). All 10 genes will be tested; GENE1, GENE3, GENE5, GENE7, GENE9 show ~2–3-fold enrichment in treatment, while GENE2, GENE4, GENE6, GENE8, GENE10 show minimal differences (expected background noise for platform validation).

workflow_ga.name: nf-core/differentialabundance
workflow_ga.description: Requires pre-computed gene/transcript count matrix as input. Does NOT process raw FASTQ files (use nf-core/rnaseq for that). Downstream differential abundance/expression analysis starting from a pre-computed count matrix. Input: gene count matrix (from nf-core/rnaseq, DESeq2, STAR, featureCounts, etc.) OR h5ad AnnData files from scRNA-seq (Seurat, scanpy). Supports single-cell RNA-seq h5ad input with cell type annotation and per-cluster or per-condition comparisons. Performs: differential expression (DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom), gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA, fgsea), volcano plots, heatmaps, pathway analysis (MSigDB, KEGG, Reactome), PCA/MDS, contrasts between conditions/treatment groups. Use this when you already have a counts table or annotated h5ad and need DE stats, GSEA, or pathway enrichment. Handles both bulk RNA-seq count matrices and pre-processed single-cell count data. Use when you already have a count matrix or h5ad and want to find enriched pathways, enriched pathways in disease condition, identify genes upregulated in disease vs control, treatment vs untreated enrichment, pathway enrichment analysis, GSEA from counts table. Typical question: 'I have a counts table — which pathways are enriched in the disease condition?' Also used for: Affymetrix microarray differential expression analysis from CEL files (after RMA/vsn normalization to count matrix), proteomics differential abundance from MaxQuant or Proteome Discoverer output.

data_requirements.min_replicates: ≥2 biological replicates per group (≥3 strongly recommended for FDR control)
data_requirements.input_format: Raw integer count matrix: genes × samples (not normalized values)
data_requirements.must_not_use: TPM, FPKM, RPKM, or any library-size-normalized values as input
data_requirements.coverage: ≥5–10M uniquely mapped reads per sample recommended; <1M is problematic
data_requirements.sparsity: Works best with bulk RNA-seq; for highly sparse data (sc) use sfType='poscounts'

key_assumptions: Count data follows negative binomial distribution with variance-mean dependence
Each factor has exactly two levels/states

common_pitfalls.fix: You must have ≥2 biological replicates per group
